title: Linux.Proxy.10_Incident_Response_Scenario_ceb
description: Investigate and respond to a potential compromise on a victim host exhibiting unusual behavior.
outcomes: Usage of systemd timers and services
Locating hidden directories and unusual file paths

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected network connections and suspicious scheduled tasks. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential compromise.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- IP Address: 192.168.60.10
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Investigate the suspicious scheduled tasks on the victim host. Identify and analyze any unauthorized or suspicious scheduled tasks that may be related to the malware.
levels.solution: Check the systemd timers and services that are running on the system. Look for any suspicious or unauthorized tasks, such as those related to the trojan. The flag is network-diagnostics.timer.

hints.title: First Hint
hints.content: Check the systemd timers and services that are running on the system.

hints.title: Second Hint
hints.content: Look for any suspicious or unauthorized tasks, such as those related to the trojan.

levels.title: Locate Files Installed by the Malware
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the compromised host. Find any files that were introduced by the trojan and analyze their contents.
levels.solution: Look for hidden directories and unusual file paths that may contain malware components. Check directories like /usr/local/lib/.netd and /var/lib/.netd. The flag is /var/lib/.netd/install.log.

hints.title: First Hint
hints.content: Look for hidden directories and unusual file paths that may contain malware components.

levels.title: Determine the External Host Communicating with the Compromised System
levels.content: Determine the external host communicating with the compromised system. Analyze network connections to identify the command-and-control server.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and logs to find any suspicious outbound connections. Look for connections to the C2 server at 192.168.60.20 on ports 18902 and 5555. The flag is 192.168.60.20.

hints.title: First Hint
hints.content: Check the network connections and logs to find any suspicious outbound connections.

hints.title: Second Hint
hints.content: Look for connections to the C2 server at 192.168.60.20 on ports 18902 and 5555.
